text:
sam: Heads-up — customer (acme-inc) seeing duplicate data chunks + early stream close with Python SDK after upgrading to 0.9.6. They get partial output, then on reconnect the server re-sends the last few chunks and the app shows duplicate content. Escalating because this affects billing and UX. Logs and repro below.

anya: Can you paste a minimal repro and confirm exact SDK version + Python version? Any token refreshes / auth rotation around the time this happened?

sam: Repro (minimal):
```py
# repro.py
import asyncio
from redwood import RedwoodClient

async def reader():
    client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")
    stream = client.stream(model="gpt-redwood-1.2", input="long prompt")
    try:
        async for chunk in stream:
            print(chunk)
            await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        # simulate client timeout/cancel
        pass

async def main():
    t = asyncio.create_task(reader())
    await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
    t.cancel()  # cancel while stream in-flight
    try:
        await t
    except Exception:
        pass
    # reopen stream immediately
    # sometimes server resends last pieces and we see duplicates

asyncio.run(main())
```
SDK v0.9.6, python 3.11.

matt: Can you paste the raw logs from both the client and the server side? Need to see SSE event ids and whether we get a proper `event: close` or just a TCP FIN. Also what region / deployment?

sam: Client debug logs (sanitized):
```
DEBUG redwood.sse > connected to stream /v1/stream
DEBUG redwood.sse < event: data id=42
DEBUG redwood.sse < {"delta": "Hello"}
DEBUG redwood.sse < event: data id=43
DEBUG redwood.sse < {"delta": " world"}
DEBUG redwood.sse > client cancelled (task.cancel) -> closing iterator
DEBUG redwood.sse > sending abort/close to runtime
INFO redwood.sse < connection closed by peer, code=1000
DEBUG redwood.sse > reconnecting with resume=true
DEBUG redwood.sse < event: data id=43
DEBUG redwood.sse < {"delta": " world"}  <-- duplicate chunk received
```
Server logs show a gap/timeout at the same time and a reconnect assigned to a new worker.

ryan: This smells like a race where the iterator cancel path triggers a premature client-side ACK or close that doesn't fully drain KV/prefix state, so on reconnect the server thinks last ack wasn't received and replays. IIRC 0.9.6 introduced a change to iterator.close becoming async that might have created a window where we drop the in-flight token counter.

anya: Customer worried about billing. If server replays tokens on reconnect, will they be double-charged? We need to confirm billing semantics for replayed chunks. @matt can you check whether billing deduplication exists for streamed tokens?

sam: I also saw one case where token refresh happened ~55s after stream open (our refresh window). The reconnect sometimes coincides with refresh handshake, so there might be overlap: cancel + token rotation -> reconnect -> duplicate.

matt: Assigned to eng-runtime to triage; filing a short repro task. @ryan can you attach a pointer to the commit that changed iterator.close? I'll grep history. Also please include the exact model variant and whether this was a hosted or dedicated deployment.

sam: Model: gpt-redwood-1.2 (hosted-us-east), no dedicated capacity. Repro reproducible locally for me on macOS with py3.11. I have a gist with the repro script and full DEBUG logs: https://gist.github.com/redwood/repro-1845123456 (private).

ellie: Marking P2; customer impact: partial outputs + duplicates cause major UX regression for their chat feature. They asked for either a patched SDK or a documented workaround.

ryan: Short-term workaround: avoid task.cancel while iterating. Instead, drain one final chunk and call `await stream.aclose()` or use a graceful cancel helper: `await asyncio.wait_for(read_all(stream), timeout)` and in timeout handler do `await stream.aclose()`. Downgrading to 0.9.5 also avoids the regression.

sam: I confirmed downgrade to 0.9.5 eliminates duplicates in my local test. Workaround instructions I gave the customer: set RW_SDK_LOG_LEVEL=debug, downgrade to 0.9.5, or apply graceful close pattern.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollback scheduled: sdk/0.9.6 -> 0.9.5 for python client (partial rollout) pending approval.

anya: Action items:
- sam: provide deterministic repro gist + exact DEBUG logs (owner)
- matt (eng-runtime): investigate runtime state machine on cancel + reconnect; check replay/dedup semantics (owner)
- ryan (eng-ml): confirm commit that changed iterator.close behavior and propose patch for safe-close (owner)
- support: verify billing duplication with eng-billing if server replay leads to chargeable tokens (owner: anya)

support-bot: Created internal ticket INC-2028-452 (priority P2). Please update ticket with analysis and customer note.

sam: Uploaded repro + logs to the ticket and sent customer the temporary workaround steps. I'll keep this thread updated with any new findings.

matt: I'll start by adding extra guards in the streaming state machine to ensure in-flight counters are decremented on CancelledError paths and add end-to-end test that simulates concurrent cancel + token refresh. Will update INC-2028-452 with patch ETA.

support-bot: Closing action checklist until next update.
